spec.description: Query the earthquake catalog by time, magnitude and location, and get the matches as GeoJSON.

request.title: EventQueryRequest
request.description: What to match, and how much of it to return.

format.description: Response format. Only `geojson` is representable here; the service also serves QuakeML, CSV, KML and plain text, which a JSON-validating client cannot read.

starttime.description: Earliest origin time to include, UTC. Inclusive.

endtime.description: Latest origin time to include, UTC. Inclusive.

latitude.description: Latitude of the centre of a circular search area, in decimal degrees. Requires `maxradiuskm`.

longitude.description: Longitude of the centre of a circular search area, in decimal degrees. Requires `maxradiuskm`.

maxradiuskm.description: Radius of the circular search area around `latitude`/`longitude`, in kilometres.

minlatitude.description: Southern edge of a rectangular search area, in decimal degrees.

maxlatitude.description: Northern edge of a rectangular search area, in decimal degrees.

minlongitude.description: Western edge of a rectangular search area, in decimal degrees.

maxlongitude.description: Eastern edge of a rectangular search area, in decimal degrees.

mindepth.description: Shallowest depth to include, in kilometres.

maxdepth.description: Deepest depth to include, in kilometres.

orderby.description: Sort order of the returned events.

limit.description: Most events to return. Sending it removes `metadata.count` from the answer; see the notes.

offset.description: Row to start at, counting from 1. Not from 0; see the notes.

unverified.detail: Written from the FDSN event service documentation and the live service's own shape, with no recording committed yet. The Record workflow replays `examples/*.request.json` through a client generated from this spec and fills in the responses.

notes: This endpoint paginates, and no `pagination` block is declared, on purpose (authoring rule 8's "omission is not a lie the checker can catch"). Two facts block every strategy the format can state: `offset` counts from 1, and an `offset` walk starts at 0 with no way to say otherwise; and `metadata.count` is replaced by `limit`/`offset` the moment `limit` is sent, so a `total` terminator would raise on a walk's every page. `short_page` on `limit` alone would be declarable, and would also be the only thing the block said, so it is left out rather than half-stated. Do not "complete" this block without re-probing both facts.
`format` is required rather than defaulted: without it the service answers QuakeML, an XML document, and a client that validates JSON would fail on the first call rather than on the spec.
Bound inclusivity is USGS's own documented behaviour, restated here rather than probed: an endpoint's inclusivity is not a spec fact and nothing checks it.

A single event is fetched by its own `detail` URL, or by `eventid` on this service, which answers with a bare Feature rather than a FeatureCollection. That is a different response shape, so it is a different endpoint, and it is not specced here.
